# Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js TypeScript Application

## Project Structure
```
project/
├── src/
│   └── index.ts
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── Dockerfile
```

## Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# ============================================================
# Stage 1: Base — shared foundation with common configuration
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS base

# Set working directory for all subsequent stages
WORKDIR /app

# Install dumb-init for proper signal handling and PID 1 management
# This ensures graceful shutdowns work correctly in containers
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# ============================================================
# Stage 2: Dependencies — install ALL dependencies (dev + prod)
# ============================================================
FROM base AS dependencies

# Copy only package files first to leverage Docker layer caching.
# If package files haven't changed, this layer is reused on rebuild.
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install all dependencies including devDependencies needed for TypeScript compilation.
# --frozen-lockfile ensures reproducible installs matching package-lock.json exactly.
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile

# ============================================================
# Stage 3: Builder — compile TypeScript to JavaScript
# ============================================================
FROM dependencies AS builder

# Copy TypeScript configuration
COPY tsconfig.json ./

# Copy source code
COPY src/ ./src/

# Compile TypeScript to JavaScript.
# Output goes to /app/dist as configured in tsconfig.json.
RUN npm run build

# ============================================================
# Stage 4: Production Dependencies — install only prod packages
# ============================================================
FROM base AS production-dependencies

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install ONLY production dependencies, excluding devDependencies.
# This creates a clean, minimal node_modules for the final image.
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile --omit=dev

# ============================================================
# Stage 5: Final — minimal production image
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS final

# Re-install dumb-init in the final stage (base stage not inherited here)
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# Create a non-root user and group for security best practices.
# Running as root inside a container is a security risk.
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 --ingroup nodejs appuser

WORKDIR /app

# Copy production node_modules from the production-dependencies stage.
# This avoids carrying over devDependencies into the final image.
COPY --from=production-dependencies --chown=appuser:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy compiled JavaScript output from the builder stage.
# Only the dist/ folder is needed — no TypeScript source or compiler.
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:nodejs /app/dist ./dist

# Copy package.json for runtime metadata (version, name, etc.)
COPY --chown=appuser:nodejs package.json ./

# Switch to non-root user before running the application
USER appuser

# Document the port the application listens on (informational)
EXPOSE 3000

# Set NODE_ENV to production for performance optimizations
# (e.g., Express disables verbose error messages, enables caching)
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Health check to verify the application is running correctly.
# Adjust the URL/port to match your application's health endpoint.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000/health', (r) => { process.exit(r.statusCode === 200 ? 0 : 1) })" \
    || exit 1

# Use dumb-init as the entrypoint to handle signals properly.
# It acts as PID 1 and forwards signals to the Node.js process.
ENTRYPOINT ["dumb-init", "--"]

# Start the compiled application
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

## Supporting Files

### tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": false,
    "sourceMap": false,
    "removeComments": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist"]
}
```

### package.json
```json
{
  "name": "my-ts-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Node.js TypeScript application",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --project tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/index.js",
    "dev": "ts-node src/index.ts",
    "lint": "eslint src/**/*.ts",
    "test": "jest"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/express": "^4.17.21",
    "@types/node": "^20.10.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.2"
  }
}
```

### .dockerignore
```
# Dependencies (will be installed fresh in Docker)
node_modules/

# Build output (will be compiled fresh in Docker)
dist/

# Version control
.git/
.gitignore

# Development files
.env.local
.env.development
*.log
npm-debug.log*

# Test files
**/*.test.ts
**/*.spec.ts
coverage/
jest.config.*

# Editor files
.vscode/
.idea/
*.swp
*.swo

# OS files
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db

# Docker files (no need to copy into image)
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
docker-compose*.yml

# Documentation
README.md
docs/
```

## Build and Run Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Build with no cache (force full rebuild)
docker build --no-cache -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Run the container
docker run -p 3000:3000 my-ts-app:latest

# Run with environment variables
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://... \
  -e API_KEY=secret \
  my-ts-app:latest

# Inspect image size
docker image inspect my-ts-app:latest --format='{{.Size}}' | \
  awk '{printf "%.2f MB\n", $1/1024/1024}'

# Compare stage sizes during development
docker build --target builder -t my-ts-app:builder .
docker build --target final   -t my-ts-app:final .
docker images my-ts-app
```

## Stage Summary

```
┌─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage                   │ Purpose                                          │
├─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ base                    │ Shared Alpine foundation + dumb-init             │
│ dependencies            │ All deps (dev + prod) for compilation            │
│ builder                 │ TypeScript → JavaScript compilation              │
│ production-dependencies │ Only production deps (no devDependencies)        │
│ final                   │ Minimal image: compiled JS + prod node_modules   │
└─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

What's EXCLUDED from the final image:
  ✗ TypeScript source files (src/)
  ✗ TypeScript compiler (typescript package)
  ✗ devDependencies (@types/*, ts-node, etc.)
  ✗ tsconfig.json
  ✗ Test files and configuration
```

## Key Optimizations Explained

| Technique | Benefit |
|-----------|---------|
| `node:20-alpine` base | ~180MB vs ~1GB for full Debian image |
| Multi-stage build | Compiler and dev tools never reach final image |
| `npm ci --frozen-lockfile` | Reproducible, faster installs |
| `--omit=dev` in final deps | Strips all devDependencies |
| `.dockerignore` | Prevents local `node_modules` from polluting build context |
| Non-root user | Security hardening |
| `dumb-init` | Correct signal handling, prevents zombie processes |
| `sourceMap: false` | Smaller compiled output |
| `COPY package files first` | Maximizes layer cache reuse |
